summary:
Raconteur examines European anxiety about a US-controlled tech "kill switch" and finds a large gap between sovereignty ambition and operational readiness.

Survey evidence: A Proton survey reports 74% of British, German and French companies fear severe disruption if American Big Tech cut off critical digital infrastructure, roughly the same share that fear a cyberattack. Yet 54% of European companies could not stay operational for more than a day without cloud access; only 28% have a cloud outage continuity solution and just 24% have continuity plans for losing access to their usual AI tools. Two thirds say they would switch providers if a foreign government restricted an essential digital service.

Vendor view: Proton COO Raphael Auphan says 56% of European firms let geopolitical risk drive purchasing decisions, and that geopolitical issues now carry the same boardroom weight as cyber risk, citing the withdrawal of Fable 5 and the denial of Microsoft services to ICC officials. Proton reports signups up nearly 80% in the Nordics, and buyers arriving with structured dependency-reduction roadmaps stretching up to 24 months. He frames the question as how fast migration happens, not whether.

Analyst counterpoint: Penny Naas of The German Marshall Fund argues US cloud and tech providers will keep dominating Europe because they invest more in R&D and offer global scale; EU cloud providers are increasingly niche, with even the largest holding under 2% of the European market, while US rivals invest tenfold in R&D and data centres. Microsoft alone invested 3.2bn euros in German data centres over two years versus just under 2bn euros from the entire German cloud industry. She cites permitting, energy prices and chip access, but says the core problem is insufficient European private investment.

Philipp Eckhardt of the Centre for European Policy sees no significant shift, blaming reluctance to adopt less competitive alternatives, cognitive dissonance about kill-switch exposure, and a free-rider dynamic. The EU Technological Sovereignty Package may shift things only over the medium term.
